Every statement of behaviour in this part is normative: a key word marks its requirement level, and a statement carrying none binds as one carrying MUST.

**A draft's store opens under that draft alone.** While this part is a draft, a program of any profile MUST refuse a store whose `format_version` is not its own draft's name, naming both, and a store lacking the column, which a draft before storage-draft-08 wrote.

A program refusing a store for its `format_version` MUST say, by this order, which of the two is the earlier, and what that asks: a store below its own was written by an earlier engine, whose queued writes it alone holds, so the user syncs it with that engine until nothing is queued, then moves its directory aside and syncs a new store; a store above its own asks for a later program.
The two MUST agree; a store where they disagree is corrupt.

**A store above a program's version is judged by `store_meta` alone.** A released reader or producer opening a store whose `version` is above its own MUST judge it by six columns of `store_meta` and by nothing else of the schema: `format` is `pimdir`; `format_version` is `storage-v` followed by `version`, a draft's name being refused; `version` equals `PRAGMA user_version`; `read_version`, and for a producer `produce_version` too, is at most its own version; `hash_algo` is one it knows (§6 step 2).

Such a program MUST NOT refuse the store, nor read it as corrupt, for a `user_version` above its own, nor for a table, a column, an index, a trigger or a view it does not know: a later version's schema is not its own to verify, and its statements name their columns (§4.4), so what that version added moves nothing they read or write.

column3: **A name is never a path.** An implementation MUST check a name against the alphabet and the length before it builds a path from it, wherever it read the name: a row, a payload, a directory entry, a remote's answer.

Where the platform allows it, it MUST NOT follow a symbolic link when it opens a shard directory or a blob (`O_NOFOLLOW`, with `O_DIRECTORY` through `openat` for the directory, or `lstat` before the open): a link found where either belongs holds no body, and an owner moves it into quarantine/ as §7 moves a body failing its name.

**An exclusive create and copy** is the one move that is not atomic, and a writer MAY use it only where no atomic no-replace move is offered or allowed (on Android before API 30, or where `renameat2` refuses `RENAME_NOREPLACE`): the final name created with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL`, which fails when the name exists, a link included; the temporary's bytes copied into it; the file `fsync`ed; then the temporary unlinked.

**A name held is verified.** When the final name exists, the writer MUST verify the file already there against its name (§7) before it keeps it, and so MUST a writer that skips its write because it finds the name or its row there.

**Reference counting**: `objects.refcount` MUST equal the number of pointers at the object across `items.object`, `items.conflict_object`, `bindings.base_object`, `bindings.conflict_object`, `bindings.shared_object` and `queue.object`, each its `id`, maintained in the same transaction as the writes, a producer's enqueue included (`pin_object`, §15.1).

A reader SHOULD open a blob so; an unlink the collector cannot make is left for the next collection, the row being gone already, and a write meeting a name still taken fails and is tried again, as any other failure of the move.

A store §4.2 says the program does not open MUST be refused, naming both versions: a draft's store under another draft or a release, a store lacking `format_version`, a released store above the highest version the implementation knows.
So MUST a store whose `hash_algo` the implementation does not know, naming it (§7).

column3: An owner at an earlier revision than the store's derives as it knows, and MUST record its own revision with `set_derivation` in the transaction of its first write of a summary, an address or a sort key: the store's rows then stand under the earlier revision, and the next owner at a later one re-derives them.

**A body is checked against its name when read.** Whoever reads a body whole (a reader, a producer, an owner, an engine, an indexer, a performer) MUST verify that its bytes hash to its name before it serves, parses, indexes, pushes or copies it, or performs an intent with it.

**A range is verified by a whole read.** Whoever serves, parses or copies part of a body (an attachment opened by offset, a message's head) MUST first read the whole file through the descriptor it reads the part from, and verify it.

**A mismatch is quarantined, never unlinked.** An owner finding a body that fails its name MUST move the file out of objects/ into quarantine/ (§3), under its name, a period and a suffix unique to the move, so one quarantined file never replaces another, and report it.
It MUST NOT unlink it: the bytes may be the only copy of something a person can still recover.
An engine MUST NOT push a body it has not verified in the run: a create or an edit whose body fails stays pending and is reported.
An owner MUST hold an exclusive advisory lock on owner.lock for as long as it owns the store.
An owner that cannot take it MUST fail immediately, naming the store, and never wait: what to do next is the caller's.

**A lock file stays.** A lock file, once created, MUST NOT be removed, renamed nor replaced while the store exists, by any program: a lock belongs to the open file, so a process opening a new file at the path would take a lock the holder of the old one does not exclude, and two owners would write one store.

An owner SHOULD verify, before each write transaction, that the file it holds locked is still the one at the path (on Unix, `fstat` on its descriptor and `stat` on the path answering one device and one inode), and give up the store, writing nothing more, when it is not.
Every lock this standard names (owner.lock and objects.lock here, index.lock in SEARCH.md) MUST be taken whole-file on the open file:
An implementation MUST NOT use `fcntl` or `lockf` record locks for them: on Linux those do not see a `flock` lock, and a process loses them when it closes any descriptor of the file.

On macOS, `fsync` stops at the drive's cache, and so does SQLite's own sync under §4.1's `synchronous` unless `PRAGMA fullfsync = ON` is set, which an owner and a producer there SHOULD set; blobs are flushed as §5 says.

The lock excludes other processes and nothing inside its own, so an owner MUST serialise its own collector against its own writers, and MUST release and retake the role as one operation, or it locks itself out.
A reader MUST NOT take either lock.
**Producers** perform the §15 enqueue transaction and nothing else, and MUST NOT assume when the owner applies it.
A producer MUST hold the staging lock on objects.lock shared across the blob write and the enqueue that pins it: that is the window a collector must not run inside.

Such a store MUST be owned by exactly one process on one host, SHOULD be enforced single-instance with a lease, and MUST use rollback-journal mode or `PRAGMA locking_mode = EXCLUSIVE`, never WAL's shared memory or `mmap`.

**Copies.** A backup MUST copy pimdir.db consistently, through SQLite's online backup API or `VACUUM INTO`, never as a file under a running owner, and then objects/ and quarantine/, whose files may be the only copy of a body (§7), and local/ (§3), holding the staging lock shared across the copies, though it writes nothing, so no collector unlinks a body the copied database names (§5).
A live store MUST NOT be replicated by a file-synchronisation tool: each host would hold an owner lock of its own over its own copy, and the tool would copy the database and its WAL mid-write.
A hint beginning with any of the six, compared byte for byte, MUST be escaped before the table below: the key is `esc:` followed by the hint (`esc:hash:0123`).

**Assigning the key.** A writer naming a member a source lists or fetches (SYNC.md §6), or staging a create (SYNC.md §7), MUST take its `link_id` from the first row of this table that matches what holds `k` in the collection.
It is opaque: a reader MUST NOT parse it and a store MUST NOT rewrite it, since rewriting would change a `seq` a consumer has shown.
Such a key MUST NOT match in `lookup_objects` and MUST NOT share a `seq` (§9.1), and no reference names one (§14.2), nor a file of a part of a message under one (§14.3).

An `attachment` reference from the message (§14.2) ties them, and the owner MUST record the file and that reference in one transaction.

A producer MAY enqueue several actions in one transaction, each on the terms above, its body stored and pinned before its `enqueue_action`: all of them are appended or none, in the order enqueued, which their ids keep.

**A run of actions in one transaction.** An owner MAY apply a bounded run of pending actions in one transaction, in ascending `id`, each under a savepoint of its own: the savepoint opens, `claim_action` runs first in it, the action is applied, its receipt recorded, and the savepoint released.

A failed apply MUST be rolled back before anything else, which restores the claimed row and undoes whatever the apply wrote: its transaction, or in a run its savepoint alone, the actions applied before it standing.
A failure of the store itself (a refused rebind, a constraint, a target collection with no declared kind) is permanent for the row and MUST park it.
Only a failure of the environment (the database busy, a body unreadable) is retried, and neither MUST stop the rows behind it.
An `add` or an `update` whose body cannot be read (its blob missing, failing to read or failing its name, §7) MUST be retried, then parked once the owner's bound on attempts is reached.
It MUST NOT be applied without its body.

An `update` or a `remove` meeting a conflict, the item's or that of the binding it runs through, MUST be parked naming the conflict unless it is a resolution naming it, and one stating `resolves` and meeting none MUST be parked too (§15.3): applying either would settle a conflict nobody decided, or one decided over another body.

column3: **An intent whose outcome is unknown.** A performer that sent an intent's request and cannot tell whether it took effect (a submission whose connection dropped once the message was handed over) MUST park the row with an `error` beginning with the reserved prefix `unconfirmed: `, the text after it free (§13), which is `unconfirm_action(id, detail)`: the attempt counted, the prefix written by the statement before `detail`, the id of the row answered.

column3: It MUST NOT perform it again of its own accord: the effect may be made, and a second one is not undone.

**Skipping is not parking.** An owner that does not recognise an action, does not know the payload version `v` a row states for an action it knows, or does not run the source an intent names, MUST leave the row pending and untouched (`error` `NULL`, `attempts` unbumped) and MUST NOT block later actions on it.

**A payload is valid whole, malformed or unknown.** A payload whose action and `v` an implementation knows is typed by their schema: one missing a member its schema requires, stating one of another type, or holding a member its version does not define is malformed: a producer MUST NOT enqueue it, and an owner knowing its action and version MUST park it, an intent's performer likewise, never applying it in part nor ignoring a member.
One beginning with `hash:` names bytes (§9): it MUST be the one the object's own bytes give (Annex A.2, A.3).

A producer MUST refuse an `add` stating a `hash:` key another body gives, read from the body it stores before anything is appended, and an owner MUST park one (§15.2), the key naming no bytes the store holds under it.
A producer changing a set it read SHOULD state it.
A row stating `base` and meeting an item whose flag set is unknown MUST be parked: there is no set to add to nor remove from, and replacing would write the unread flags as removed.
column5: §15.3 Actions: the flag set's being unknown reads items.flags_known 0 (marks 0, keywords '')

column3: `if_match` is the body the producer read and deletes: when the item's current body is another, or the item holds none, the owner MUST park the row, naming both, the delete having been decided over a body the item no longer holds.
A producer deleting a mutable item it read SHOULD state it; a row without it removes whatever the item holds.

A remove meeting a conflict, the item's or that of the binding it runs through, MUST be parked, naming the conflict, unless `resolves` names the `conflict_object` of each conflict it meets; one stating `resolves` and meeting none MUST be parked.
A producer MUST NOT state `resolves` on any other remove.

A `move` whose target is the collection the item is in MUST be parked, naming it, and a producer MUST NOT enqueue one: applied, it would tombstone the item and stage a create beside it under a minted key (SYNC.md §7), which for an item held without its body never delivers while the tombstone pushes a delete.

A `move` meeting a conflict, the item's or that of the binding it runs through, MUST be parked, naming the conflict: a `move` states no `resolves`, so it is never a person's resolution, and the diverging body would stay pinned under the tombstone it leaves, where nobody is shown it.

When the item's current body is another, or the item holds none (a pull having emptied it, SYNC.md §5), the owner MUST park the row, naming both, an absent body as none: the body the producer read is not what the item holds, and applying the row would drop another write without a merge (SYNC.md §7).
A producer editing a body it read SHOULD state it; a row without it applies over whatever the item holds.

A producer deciding a conflict (a resolution command or form) states it, and MUST NOT state it on any other update: an ordinary edit, written before a conflict arose or without it in view, never settles one.

One meeting a conflict MUST be parked, naming the conflict, unless `resolves` names the `conflict_object` of each conflict it meets; one stating `resolves` and meeting none MUST be parked, the conflict it was decided over being settled already.
A key under `pimdir/` other than `pimdir/label` is malformed by the schema: a producer MUST NOT enqueue one, and an owner writes none (§4.3).

The owner reads the body from the column and never builds a path from the payload: a row whose payload's `object` is not the hash the column names, the column `NULL` included, MUST be parked, naming both.
**An item no source binds** is the store's alone to settle: an owner MUST apply or park an action naming it, never skip it, since nothing would ever bind it for the row's sake.
An application MAY carry further ones; the store owes them append order, blob pinning and the skip rule.
A reader MAY overlay a collection's pending actions (`load_pending_actions`) for read-your-writes.

An overlay SHOULD fold a row as the owner would apply it to the rows the reader sees: a `set-flags` stating `base` as the change it is, over the set the item shows; a `set-property` as the change it is, over the properties the item shows (`list_item_properties`), its removes then its adds, a label compared folded; and nothing for a row the owner would park (§15.2, §15.3, §15.6), among them a `set-flags` stating `base` over an unknown set, a `set-property` naming a `seq` no live row of its collection holds or leaving more than 64 values under its key, an `update` or a `remove` whose `if_match` names another body than the item shows, the item showing none included, or one meeting a conflict its `resolves` does not name, or a `move` meeting a conflict or into the collection its item is in, and an action on an item no source binds that the rules above park.

A row found in neither was cancelled by request (§15.5), or applied longer ago than its receipt is kept: the owner keeps a receipt at least seven days after `applied_at`, and while a refusal stands on its item, then MAY drop it (`prune_receipts`).
column5: §15.4 Reading the queue: prune_receipts named in io-pimdir

column3: It is an owner write and MUST run in one transaction with `release_pins` on what it returned.
column5: §15.5 Cancelling and acknowledging: reads "the row deleted and its pin released in one transaction"; cancel_action and release_pins named in io-pimdir

column3: A performer acknowledging an intent it performed MUST record the intent's receipt (`record_receipt`) in that same transaction: its `id`, the collection it was queued on and, as `seq`, the item its effect left in the store when the performer knows it, `NULL` otherwise (a collection created, which arrives with a later sync; a message sent, its copy filed by the provider).
A declaration MUST write every capability of Annex B's base set the owner knows of the kinds the source syncs, `none` included, so a source supporting nothing still says so.
**The producer's gate.** Before it enqueues, a producer SHOULD resolve the capabilities the action needs against the sources concerned.
A `partial` support passes and its detail SHOULD be shown.
Otherwise the producer MUST NOT choose: it refuses, listing the candidates, and the user picks, for this action alone or durably through `set-performer` (§15.3).

An action reaching the drain needing a capability (Annex B, `calendar.component.vtodo` included) that a declared source concerned does not support, or an intent whose `source` does not declare its capability, MUST be parked with the capability and the source named in `error`.

A summary vector states a row as the model holds it, its lists (`in_reply_to`, `categories`) as arrays though the store keeps them as rows, and a consumer MUST compare parsed structures, never JSON text.
column5: §16 Test vectors: the store keeps those lists as summary_value rows

column3: Every file under vectors/ states the version of its format as a top-level `v` and conforms to the JSON Schema of that format under vectors/schema/, which checks/vectors.py validates; an implementation meeting a `v` it does not know MUST NOT read the file as a version it knows.
An implementation that vendors vectors/ SHOULD record their digests and re-check them against this repository in its CI, since a frozen copy keeps passing while the format moves.

It MUST meet every section its row names, keep §4.4's terms for the statements of its directories, each run under its canonical name or its effect reached through statements of its own, and pass the vectors its row names, and MUST state its conformance as each part's version and the profile it meets there, the layers' by SYNC.md §12 and SEARCH.md §12: `storage-draft-16 owner, sync-draft-15 engine, search-draft-16 indexer (canonical)`.
column5: §17 Conformance: restated without "keep §4.4's terms for the statements of its directories" and without the "(own statement text)" tag; the profile table loses its Statements column

column3: **Modes.** A program creating a store MUST create its directory, objects/, its shard directories and quarantine/ with mode `0700` and every file in them `0600`, index.db, the lock files and SQLite's `-wal` and `-shm` included, as an owner creates local/ and what it keeps there (§3), or on Windows with an ACL granting its own user alone.
A program opening a store whose directory or pimdir.db another user can read or write SHOULD refuse it, or open it only once the user confirms.
An owner MAY ask the user before it performs an intent another process queued (a message sent, an invitation answered).
A lock file MUST be opened without following a symbolic link (`O_NOFOLLOW`, `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` on Windows), a link there failing the open and naming the store.

A program deriving a filesystem path from one, saving an attachment or mirroring a folder, MUST neutralise in it every path separator (`/`, and `\` where the platform reads one), a `.` or `..` component, NUL, every control character (U+0001 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F) and every bidirectional formatting character (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069), and MUST NOT write outside the directory it chose.

A producer enqueuing an `add` or an `update` of a resource the user did not write as it stands (an invitation added to a calendar, an imported file, a resource copied from a message) MUST first remove every such property from it, writing one only as the user asks.

**No credential in the store.** No program writes a password, a token, a cookie or any other credential into a column of the store or of the index, the opaque ones included (`checkpoint`, `round_cursor`, `round_checkpoint`, `queue.producer`, `queue.error`, `capabilities.detail`, `retained_by`, `bindings.refusal`, a property's value, `pimdir/session-key` included until a version of this part defines it), and text it records from an error or a remote's refusal MUST first be scrubbed of the credentials it may carry (a URL's userinfo, an `Authorization` header, a token in a query string).

A program opening a store it did not create (a copy received, a backup someone else made) SHOULD open both with `PRAGMA trusted_schema = OFF` and `SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DEFENSIVE`, which the canonical schemas and statements run under, each where its SQLite offers it: the pragma from SQLite 3.31, `SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DEFENSIVE` from 3.26.
column5: §18 Security considerations: "which the canonical schemas and statements run under" reads "which the store schema runs under"

column3: Below 3.31, the 3.18 floor of §4.1 among them, nothing keeps a crafted trigger or view from calling a function the program registers, so such a program SHOULD instead read `sqlite_master` before any other statement and refuse the store when it holds a trigger or a view whose text the canonical schema at the store's version does not create, naming it, and SHOULD register no SQL function with a side effect on the connection.

That comparison is made against a version the program knows and against no other: a store above its version (§4.2) holds triggers and views it cannot tell from crafted ones, so below 3.31 a reader or a producer SHOULD refuse such a store it did not create, or open it only once the user confirms, while from 3.31 the pragma needs no comparison and the store opens as §4.2 says.

A value such a summary serves raw, as the content carries it, is derived by this annex's rules and MUST then agree with the body's derivation byte for byte, the attachment mark, the size and the invitation aside.
The size and the mark read without the body are replaced by the body's own once it is read, and a writer holding the body MUST NOT write either read without it over it.
**Reading the header.** The identity and the `alt:` key are built from these parses, so every writer MUST read a header as follows.
A writer holding the body MUST NOT write such a value over the body's, as for the size and the mark.

A link id derived from one is kept once resolved (SYNC.md §6) and may differ from the key a raw reading gives, a missed dedup (§9), so a writer SHOULD read the fields of the hint raw, as a connector MUST read the three a member is compared by (SYNC.md §4).
A character assigned later, which no vector holds, MAY map as the writer's version says, a missed seek or a mis-sort being the cost.
A connector to an instance-granular source MUST reassemble the set.

A producer recording that acceptance MUST write it into the resource as `SCHEDULE-AGENT=NONE` on every `ORGANIZER` and `ATTENDEE` of the component lacking `SCHEDULE-AGENT=CLIENT` or `NONE`, never as a flag of its own: the resource is then not scheduled, the parameter living in it, so the gate and the backstop read the same answer, and a source that schedules leaves the attendees so marked alone.

A source that schedules on the server and has no verb for them MAY perform them as the write its server schedules from, a `PARTSTAT` change or a removal, and declares them `partial` when `comment` is lost.

Where the owner derives the collection's id from its name (an IMAP mailbox's), the performer SHOULD follow the rename in the store with `rename_collection` (§14) when it acknowledges the intent, so the items keep their bindings rather than leaving under the old id and arriving under the new one.
column5: Annex B.2 Intents: rename_collection reads "renames the collection in the store (§14)"

column3: An implementation MAY omit search.
One that offers it MUST conform by a profile of §12, vectors/search/ being the bar, so every client on one store answers `is:unread from:jane` the same way.

The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 (RFC 2119, RFC 8174) when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.
Every statement of behaviour in this part is normative: a key word marks its requirement level, and a statement carrying none binds as one carrying MUST.

The index MUST be a SQLite database named index.db in the store directory (STORAGE §3), `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` RECOMMENDED so query clients read while a refresh writes.
column5: SEARCH §1 Scope, a new paragraph on the index file (index.db, a SQLite file whose name STORAGE §3 reserves and whose index_meta every implementation reads); its PRAGMA foreign_keys and WAL clauses move to io-pimdir's index

column3: The **canonical shape** is [migrations/search/0001_init.sql](./migrations/search/0001_init.sql) and the statements under queries/search/, every table `STRICT`, and is the RECOMMENDED one.
column5: io-pimdir: its index schema (migrations/search/0001_init.sql, STRICT tables, SQLite 3.43 with FTS5) and its statements (queries/search/), the canonical shape becoming its own

column3: An index of another shape (FTS4, FTS3, or no full-text module) MAY answer the same language: every query's hit set is the one vectors/search/ gives, its text folded as §5 says and its text terms matched as §8.5 says.
column5: SEARCH §12 Conformance: reads "every index answers the language with the hit sets vectors/search/ gives, folding as §5 says and matching as §8.5 says"; "of another shape" goes with the canonical shape

column3: **The hit-set guarantee leaves out text reduced from HTML, and a part's text beyond seven-bit ASCII in a charset other than UTF-8.** §6 pins neither how a `text/html` part becomes text nor, but as a recommendation, how another charset is decoded, so a word that text alone holds MAY be a hit in one conforming index and not in another.
column5: SEARCH §6 Extraction, beside the HTML and charset rules it limits

column3: **An indexer rebuilds only an older index of its own shape.** An indexer MUST refuse an index.db holding no `index_meta`, one whose `shape` is not its own, and one whose `format_version` lies above its own, naming the index's version and shape and its own, and MUST NOT rebuild, write nor delete it: a person deleting index.db hands the store to another indexer, losing nothing (§1).
column5: SEARCH §1 Scope (the index file): index.db names its format, version and shape in index_meta, and an indexer leaves an index not its own untouched; two implementations meet at that file in one store directory

column3: An index of its own shape whose `format_version` lies below its own, and one whose `index_meta` lacks `format_version`, which a draft before search-draft-08 wrote and whose indexer refuses this draft's store (STORAGE §4.2), MUST be rebuilt: there are no index migrations.
column5: io-pimdir: rebuilding an older index of its own shape, there being no index migrations

column3: An index of the indexer's own shape and version MUST also be rebuilt when its `index_meta.tokenizer` differs from §5's, its schema text from 0001_init.sql's (the canonical shape), when it was built from another store or another copy of it, or when its `store_change` lies above the store's last stamp.
column5: io-pimdir: its rebuild triggers (tokenizer, schema text); the half on another store, incarnation or a stamp above the store's restates STORAGE §4.5 "A reset", kept there

column3: An indexer MUST state an `extractor`, and another one whenever a change of its own alters what the extraction of a body yields.
column5: io-pimdir: index_meta.extractor, its own revision of the extraction

column3: An indexer finding either differing from its own, the texts compared byte for byte, MUST extract again every body the index holds and expand again every calendar item, leaving what a rebuild would write, and record its own (`set_extraction`) in the transaction completing it; it MAY rebuild the index instead.
column5: io-pimdir: extracting and expanding again on a revision change (set_extraction)

column3: **A query client reads only an index it implements.** It MUST refuse an index whose `shape` or `format_version` it does not implement, naming both, rather than answer from it; while this part is a draft it implements its own draft alone, as STORAGE §4.2 has a program open only its own draft's store.
column5: SEARCH §1 Scope (the index file): a query client refuses an index whose shape or version it does not implement

column3: It is the sole writer of index.db and MUST hold an exclusive advisory lock on index.lock for a refresh, on the owner lock's terms: taken whole-file with `flock(2)` on Unix or `LockFileEx` on Windows, never an `fcntl` record lock (STORAGE §8).
column5: SEARCH §1 Scope (the index file), or STORAGE §8, which already names index.lock among the locks taken whole-file

column3: An owner keeping an index SHOULD refresh it after each write batch it commits (STORAGE §14), so a client reading its rows from the store and its filters from the index finds the two at most one batch apart.
column5: io-pimdir: when an owner refreshes its index (§4's procedure); `behind` (§8.2) stays the answer's measure of the lag

column3: summary text is written while it has no body and dropped when it gains one, in the same transaction: a placement MUST NOT hold both a body and summary text once a batch commits, so it names one document (§3);
column5: io-pimdir: one document per placement in its index (summary_text or body); §8.2 keeps that a bodiless placement matches on its summary

column3: its keywords are replaced (`replace_flags`, `insert_flag`): the flags `load_changed_items` answers but the five system flags, which the indexer MUST NOT write into `flag` (§3);
column5: io-pimdir: its `flag` table holds keywords alone; §8's table keeps that a system flag is read from the store

column3: A batch MAY record its last row's stamp (`load_changed_items` answers each row's) as `store_change` in its own transaction, the purge count left as the last completed pass recorded it.
column5: io-pimdir: a refresh batch's intermediate cursor

column3: Extraction MAY run in parallel; the index is written by one transaction per batch.
column5: io-pimdir: a refresh's parallelism and transactions

column3: Mail extraction MUST walk the MIME tree as STORAGE Annex A.1 walks it, reading every part it reads, the last child of a multipart nothing closes among them, and no part it leaves unread, an entity's own fields read from their first occurrence as A.1 reads them.
It MUST decode transfer encodings, decode each text part by its `charset`, decode RFC 2047 and RFC 2231, prefer `text/plain` and reduce `text/html` to text.

It SHOULD separate tokens at the boundaries of block-level elements, so the texts of two table cells, two paragraphs or two list items never join into one token, and SHOULD skip the content of the head, style, script and template elements whatever their attributes.

A header field the extraction reads, `Subject` and the address fields here and `In-Reply-To` and `References` in §9, MUST be read as STORAGE Annex A.1 reads one: its line split into name and value and its name matched as A.1 says, and a field present twice read from its first occurrence, so the index holds the subject and the people the summary row states, never those of a later occurrence.

A text part SHOULD be decoded as STORAGE Annex A.1 decodes an encoded word's octets, by the WHATWG Encoding Standard's decoder for the encoding its `charset` labels, no byte order mark sniffed, `us-ascii` when it states none (RFC 2046 §4.1.2), and as UTF-8 replaced as Annex A.0 says when no label names one.
A reader MUST read a status it does not know as `unparseable`: coverage counts it so (§8.2), and `is:encrypted` does not match it.
column5: SEARCH §6 Extraction: reads "an extraction status" rather than the index column object.status

column3: Extraction MUST record the chunk boundaries of the `body` and `note` fields, one `chunk` row per chunk (`insert_chunk`), numbered from 0 in text order, the `body` field's before the `note` field's, and bounded by UTF-8 byte offsets into the field's text:
column5: SEARCH §6 Extraction: the chunk boundaries stay the rule vectors/search/chunks.json pins and snippets are cut by; "one `chunk` row per chunk (`insert_chunk`)" goes with the index's chunk table (design §5)

column3: One whose extraction is not the indexer's, which `index_meta.extractor` names (§2), MUST re-chunk its own text by the rule above rather than apply the stored offsets to it.
column5: The index keeps no chunk offsets any more (design §5 drops the `chunk` table, read by nothing): every snippet is cut by chunking the client's own extraction, so no stored offsets can be misapplied

column3: A series no expander accepts (an `RRULE` with no `DTSTART`) yields no occurrence and MUST NOT fail the pass.

A re-expansion that cannot read an item's body (§4) MUST keep the occurrences and the cut the index holds for it, never replace them by none, and record its placement in `missing`, so every pass expands the item again until its body is read: the horizon, the version and the zone a pass records then stand for every item but those `missing` names.
column5: SEARCH §7 Calendar time: reads "keeps the occurrences and the cut it held, the placement counted `missing` in coverage until its body is read", the index's `missing` rows being io-pimdir's

column3: A query outside the horizon MUST say so in its coverage (§8).

An indexer whose database names another version MUST re-expand every live calendar item and record the new version (`set_tzdb_version`) in the pass that sees it: `items_to_reexpand`, bound to that version, returns every live calendar item when it is not the recorded one, the horizon bound twice when it did not roll.
column5: SEARCH §7 Calendar time: reads "occurrences stand under the time zone database the indexer runs: a new version re-expands every live calendar item"; index_meta.tzdb_version, set_tzdb_version and items_to_reexpand named in io-pimdir

column3: An indexer stating another zone than `floating_zone` records MUST likewise re-expand every live calendar item and record its zone (`set_floating_zone`) in the pass that sees it: `items_to_reexpand`, bound to the zone too, returns every live calendar item when it is not the recorded one, so two indexers in two zones never leave rows read in both.
column5: SEARCH §7 Calendar time: the same for the floating zone; the recorded zone stays what §8.2's zone coverage compares

column3: A client SHOULD state the user's zone, the one its indexer states as `floating_zone` (§7), so the days a query names and the floating times and dates the index placed agree; a query client reads it from `index_meta.floating_zone` (`load_index_meta`).
column5: SEARCH §8.1 Dates: "(`load_index_meta`)" goes, the client learning the index's zone from its implementation

column3: An implementation MAY flatten to one row per placement on request.

A hit whose public id `split` does not hold names one document (§3), so it meets any combination of text terms exactly when that document does: a count MAY match every such hit by one full-text expression over the documents, and evaluates each hit whose public id `split` holds per placement instead (`split_seqs`, then `match_object` and `match_summary`), a hit the store no longer holds never answered all the same.
column5: io-pimdir: counting through its `split` table (split_seqs, match_object, match_summary); the per-hit rule for text terms stays in §8.2

column3: `relevance`: the shape's own, best first, bm25 RECOMMENDED and the canonical shape's (FTS5 `bm25`); a shape without one MAY refuse `relevance` and say so.
column5: SEARCH §8.2 Semantics: "and the canonical shape's" goes, bm25 stays RECOMMENDED

column3: The placements of one item hold one key where the store shares a `seq` by agreement on the date (STORAGE §9.1), so a dated order is the same whichever of them is read; where they differ, an implementation MAY read the key among the placements of the query's collections, or, when two `collection:` or `folder:` conjuncts leave none, of the first one's, so a page may be cut by walking those collections in key order.

**A page.** A client MAY answer the first hits in the query's order after a cursor, the last hit it answered, rather than every hit, and every page walked to the end answers the hits and the order one whole answer does.
Its field is the text before the first colon and MUST be a name of §8's table, as written; anything else is refused (`unknown-field`).
**Wildcard.** A `*` MUST be the last character of a text or of a text field's value, after two characters or more.
A query the grammar does not accept, or whose field or value §8.3 does not know, MUST be refused whole, never answered in part nor read as free text.

vectors/search/ holds the fixture store and the queries every conforming implementation MUST answer alike, each file stating the version of its format, `v` 5 for queries.json, `v` 3 for store.json, `v` 1 for chunks.json and `v` 5 for refresh.json, and conforming to its JSON Schema under vectors/schema/:
column5: SEARCH §11 Test vectors: refresh.json loses its index internals `objects` and `split` (design §2), the files' `v` restated

column3: An implementation offering search conforms by one profile or both, stated as STORAGE §17 says with the shape it builds or reads (`search-draft-16 indexer (canonical)`, `search-draft-16 query client (canonical)`), and MUST meet every section its row names and answer the vectors it names.
column5: SEARCH §12 Conformance: the "(canonical)" shape tag of the conformance statement goes with the canonical shape
